blocks.content: The Panchayati Raj System represents rural local self-government in India. It aims to decentralize power and ensure people's participation in governance at the grassroots level. The system received constitutional status through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
1. Background of Panchayati Raj

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 accorded constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added Part IX and the 11th Schedule containing 29 functional items.
The system provides a compulsory three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level.
Gram Sabha serves as the primary foundation of the Panchayati Raj system, comprising all persons registered in the electoral rolls of the village.
Direct elections are conducted for members at all three levels, with a tenure of 5 years and a minimum age requirement of 21 years to contest.
Mandatory reservation of at least one-third (33%) of total seats is provided for women across all levels.

blocks.content: • Village self-government existed in ancient India.
• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended democratic decentralization.
• The committee suggested a three-tier Panchayati Raj system.
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayats.
2. Constitutional Provisions (Part IX)
3. Three-Tier Structure
4. Gram Sabha
• Consists of all registered voters in the village.
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions.
• Acts as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system.
• Approves plans and budgets of the Gram Panchayat.
5. Gram Panchayat
• Executive body at village level.
• Members elected directly by villagers.
• The head is called Sarpanch or Pradhan.
6. Panchayat Samiti

rows: Implementation of local grass-root development activities and civic services
Executive body coordinating development plans between Gram Panchayats and District
Advisory, supervisory, and coordinating body operating at the district level

blocks.content: • Works at block level.
• Coordinates activities of Gram Panchayats.
7. Zila Parishad
• Functions at district level.
• Supervises Panchayat Samitis.
8. Key Features of the System
• Three-tier structure of governance.
• Regular elections every five years.
• Reservation for SC, ST and women.
• State Election Commission for conducting elections.

items: Article 243D mandates reservation of not less than one-third of the total number of seats for women.
Article 243I requires the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission every 5 years to review financial position.
Article 243K vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections to Panchayats in the State Election Commission.
States having a population not exceeding 20 lakhs are exempted from constituting the intermediate (Panchayat Samiti) level.

blocks.content: • State Finance Commission for financial review.
EXAM Important Facts
• 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) introduced Panchayati Raj.
• Gram Sabha is the basic unit of rural democracy.
• At least one-third seats reserved for women.
• Panchayat elections are held every 5 years.
